display.purpose: One dashboard headline per screen at most.

title.purpose: Panel, dialog and section titles; bill name; extra-large button labels.

body.purpose: Default text, product names, table cells (Compact).

label.purpose: Field labels, tabs, segmented controls, chips (Compact). Renders Regular; SemiBold in tabs, segments, chips.

caption.purpose: Metadata, helper text, SKU lines, side-nav group labels. Floor: 12 px.

money-lg.purpose: Change, cash received, KPI tiles, extra-large pay button amount.

money.purpose: Line amounts, table cells, tile prices; right-aligned (Compact).

money-sm.purpose: Unit prices, secondary amounts, shortcut key hints.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Surfaces on the canvas: cart, tables, cards. Dark adds a 1px border-subtle edge.

shadows.name: shadow-3
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and sheets, over the scrim.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus only; never on the always-focused sell search.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: Hover/press and small state changes; the egui animation time.

motion.name: base
motion.purpose: Defined token; not yet wired to an animated surface.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: Defined token; not yet wired to an animated surface.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Product inspector docks at 340px instead of opening as a sheet.

extensions.sourceOfTruth: design/ (POS Design System v0.1); runtime: apps/pos-desktop/src/ui/tokens.rs

narrative.overview:
A warm-paper workspace: stone neutrals, dark ink, thin hairlines instead of heavy frames, and a single saffron signal that marks the action that moves money. The screen stays quiet so the cashier always knows which button comes next. Money is set in a fixed-width face, shown in full to two decimals, and right-aligned everywhere it appears.

The world draws from three explored directions. From Studio: layered surfaces, a neutral frame with one signal color, the workspace switcher, `Ctrl K`, switchable density, held bills as tabs, offline and shift status always in the top bar. From Ledger: IBM Plex Mono money, right-aligned columns, F-key hints on desktop, hairlines instead of thick frames. From Counter: a real touch density (48–64 px controls), quick-cash chips, cart steppers, and an amount due readable from a metre away.

Two independent axes shape every screen. Appearance is Light, Dark or System (follows the OS). Density is Compact (keyboard and mouse, shortcut hints visible) or Touch (larger controls and type, hints hidden). Every screen supports both input methods in both densities.
keyCharacteristics: Warm stone neutrals in both themes; saffron is the only brand hue.
One saffron primary per view, reserved for commit actions such as take payment, confirm and save.
IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Sans Thai for UI; IBM Plex Mono for every amount.
4 pt spacing grid, five radius tiers, three elevation levels.
Every action has a visible control and a keyboard shortcut.
Built-in line icons painted as vectors, always paired with a text label or tooltip.

rules.name: The One Saffron Rule
rules.body: At most one saffron primary button per view, and only for an action that commits or moves money (take payment, confirm, save). Everything else is secondary, ghost or danger.

rules.name: The Semantic Only Rule
rules.body: Screens read colors from the active `Palette` through role names. They never use `primitive` ramps or hex literals, and they never mix light and dark roles in one control.

rules.name: The Not By Color Alone Rule
rules.body: Status always pairs a hue with text (badge label, "Out · 0", "Offline"). Money stays readable without its color.

rules.name: The Whole Baht Rule
rules.body: Money is always IBM Plex Mono, shows every digit with two decimals (`1,019.00`), and is right-aligned. Never abbreviate, truncate or round it for display.

rules.name: The Density Type Rule
rules.body: Only body, label and money grow with Touch density (14→16, 13→15, 14→16). Titles, captions and the large money sizes stay fixed.

rules.name: The Both Hands Rule
rules.body: Every action has a visible control and a key. In Compact, buttons and fields show their key hint (`F9`, `F2`, `Ctrl K`) as a bordered mono chip; in Touch the hint is hidden but the key still works.

rules.name: The Dark Edge Rule
rules.body: In dark mode every surface gets a 1 px border-subtle edge. Never rely on shadow alone to separate dark planes.

dos: Do use exactly one saffron primary per view, for the commit or money-moving action.
Do read colors and sizes from `Theme` (palette, metrics, space, radius, type_scale). Change values in `design/tokens/` and regenerate.
Do set every amount in IBM Plex Mono, in full with two decimals, right-aligned in columns.
Do give every action both a visible control and a shortcut, and show the hint in Compact.
Do check every screen in Light and Dark, Compact and Touch, Thai and English, at 1000 × 700 and 1280 × 820.
Do keep keyboard focus visible with the blue ring, except for the always-focused sell search, which uses its firm border.
Do prefer undo (toast plus `Ctrl Z`) over confirmation. Confirm only irreversible actions, and state the effect in numbers.
donts: Don't use the solid saffron fill for navigation, decoration or a second button in the same view. Navigation may use only the Saffron Wash, and charts only series 1.
Don't use subtle text for information, or set any text below 12 px.
Don't separate dark surfaces by shadow alone. Keep the highlight edge.
Don't convey status by color alone.

Don't add product images, a receipt print step, or any Future-exploration surface (tables/zones, kitchen display, PromptPay QR, stock count, split tender, discounts, multi-branch) until it is designed in `design/` first.
